A mathematical expression representing equal parts of a whole unit or equal parts of a collection of objects.
A fraction whose numerator is strictly smaller than its denominator, representing a value less than 1 whole.
A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator, representing a value equal to or greater than 1 whole.
The degree of rotational movement formed between two intersecting rays or lines meeting at a common vertex.
A closed two-dimensional geometric figure bounded entirely by three or more straight line segments.

item.statement: Every prime number has exactly 2 factors (1 and itself); 1 is neither prime nor composite.
item.explanation: 2 is the smallest prime number and the only even prime number.

item.rule_statement: To compare two 5-digit numbers, compare digits starting from the leftmost place (Ten Thousands). If equal, move right to Thousands, Hundreds, Tens, and Ones.
To round to the nearest Hundred, inspect the Tens digit: if 5 or greater, round up the Hundreds digit; if less than 5, keep the Hundreds digit.
Multiplying or dividing both numerator and denominator of a fraction by the same non-zero whole number produces an equivalent fraction.
A whole number is divisible by 2 if its ones digit is even (0, 2, 4, 6, or 8).
A whole number is divisible by 5 if its ones digit is either 0 or 5.
A whole number is divisible by 10 if its ones digit is 0.
A whole number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its individual digits is divisible by 3.
To convert PM hours (1:00 PM to 11:59 PM) into 24-hour time, add 12 to the hour digit (e.g., 2:30 PM + 12 = 14:30 hours).
Every 5th tally mark must be drawn as a diagonal slash across the four preceding vertical tally marks to create a 5-unit bundle (卌).

steps: Step 1: Take any 2-digit or 3-digit starting whole number.
Step 2: Reverse the order of its digits.
Step 3: Add the original number and the reversed number together.
Step 4: Check if the sum is a palindrome. If not, repeat the reverse-and-add steps with the new sum until a palindromic number is produced.
Step 1: Decompose each multi-digit factor into Tens and Ones (e.g., 23 × 12 → (20 + 3) × (10 + 2)).
Step 2: Set up a 2×2 grid matrix with decomposed terms along headers.
Step 3: Calculate four individual cell products (20×10=200, 20×2=40, 3×10=30, 3×2=6).
Step 4: Sum all four partial products together (200 + 40 + 30 + 6 = 276).
Step 1: Write dividend and divisor in long division format.
Step 2: Estimate a friendly partial quotient (e.g., 10s, 20s, 50s) and multiply by divisor.
Step 3: Subtract product from remaining dividend.
Step 4: Repeat estimation and subtraction until remaining dividend is smaller than divisor.
Step 5: Sum all partial quotients to obtain final Quotient, with leftover as Remainder.
Step 1: Trace the closed 2D figure onto 1 cm × 1 cm square grid paper.
Step 2: Count all fully enclosed unit squares (Value = 1 sq unit each).
Step 3: Count all half unit squares and pair every two half squares as 1 full sq unit.
Step 4: Include squares that are more than half covered as 1 full sq unit, and ignore squares less than half covered.
Step 5: Sum all values to get total estimated surface area.
